title: Dynamics and Relativity (lecture notes)
institution: University of Cambridge, DAMTP (Part IA Mathematical Tripos)
description: First-year course on Newtonian mechanics and special relativity: Newtonian mechanics, forces, dimensional analysis, central forces, systems of particles, non-inertial frames, and a 54-page chapter on special relativity (Lorentz transformations, relativistic physics, the geometry of spacetime, relativistic kinematics, particle physics, spinors). About 160 pages, seven chapters, four problem sheets.
rightsNotes: The notes page states no licence and no copyright or reuse terms. Author copyright is assumed; Corniversity treats the notes as reference-only (cite and link, do not copy or ingest).
The historic DAMTP address https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/relativity.html returned a 301 redirect to davidtong.org on 2026-10-30.

Convention: Chapter 7 defines the invariant interval as Δs² = c²Δt² − Δx² − Δy² − Δz² and writes the Minkowski metric as η = diag(+1, −1, −1, −1), the opposite overall sign to Corniversity's (−,+,+,+); c is kept explicit (verified in the chapter text, Sections 7.3.1 and 7.4.7).

Section-level locators for Chapter 7 are web locators whose headings were verified in the PDF text; no page-level pdf locators are recorded because the material is reference-only.
No year is stated on the page.

Section 7.5.1, printed p.146, incorrectly describes the Higgs decay to two photons as the predominant channel. CERN identifies bottom-quark pairs as dominant; the diphoton channel is rare. PHY-210 lesson08 flags this source error and separates kinematics from branching probabilities.
